summary: I read docs/r3-panel-brief.md and docs/critic-guide.md fully, verified the checkout was a875ace (eb40 is an ancestor with only docs deltas), and inspected keyboard_mode_for/press_key, classify_press, lock input-region/pointer handling, draw_icon scaling and caption/icon tests. I ran only focused offline tests: keyboard grab, keyboard, classify_press, hit, iter27, search-band, glyph-band, toggle-disc multi-scale, and caption proportions; all passed. I did no edits, live input, capture, socket commands, or full suite. Using actual PNG pixels, current/reference uptime ink normalized to 0.173 vs 0.171 width and 0.068 vs 0.070 height, with matching RGB (~111/112 grey); Lock caption 0.061 vs 0.058 width and 0.057 vs 0.055 height. CC glyphs in the supplied 1.5x capture covered 16.5-29.3% of their discs, contrast 6.68:1 Wi-Fi and 11.95:1 others, with centroids within 1.4px horizontally of measured disc centers. Escape/Left/Right and pill exits exist for normal panels, and the lock preview is intentionally non-security. Strict verdict: not ship under this lens because the lock preview has no reachable user-facing exit. Live pointer/focus behavior and keyboard activation with the pointer inside OnDemand panels remain unverified because live input was prohibited.

findings.title: Lock preview traps the user with no reachable in-panel exit
findings.detail: Entering Lockscreen calls sync_keyboard_interactivity(), but keyboard_mode_for(Lockscreen) returns None, so the Escape branch in press_key cannot receive an event. The fullscreen lock surface gets the whole input region, yet pointer events are explicitly skipped while Lockscreen is active, and classify_press maps Lockscreen to NoOp. Exits exist only through external socket words (unlock/clock/state). Counterexample: this is a deliberately non-security preview and an external harness can recover it, so it is not a lockout blocker; however a user who opens it from the Power Lock disc has no visible, clickable, or key-operable way out. Fix: add an on-panel exit target classified before the Lockscreen NoOp, or route Escape/tap while preserving the no-real-lock preview.

findings.title: Panel controls have no keyboard focus or activation path
findings.detail: Non-typing panels use OnDemand keyboard interactivity and press_key only provides Escape/Left/Right navigation; Control Center toggles/sliders, Power buttons, Calendar chevrons and Music transport are classified from pointer coordinates but have no Tab focus ring, selected-element state, or Enter/Space activation. Counterexample: OnDemand deliberately avoids stealing typing from the focused window, normal panels have pill/Escape exits, and live pointer-inside focus was not exercised, so this is a source-level accessibility gap rather than a measured live failure. Fix: when the island already has focus, add a visible focus indicator and Enter/Space activation for classified controls without making the layer Exclusive globally; add focused tests for focus traversal and activation.

findings.title: Multi-scale icon coverage assertions cover only Bluetooth
findings.detail: draw_icon now scales both glyph size and position by scale_of(w), which fixes the prior 2x disappearance bug. The multi-scale test asserts presence, centroid and coverage for Bluetooth at 1x/1.5x/2x, but not Wi-Fi, NightLight or the procedural Focus glyph; disc roundness and a separate glyph-band test do not substitute for all-glyph centroid/coverage. Counterexample: the supplied current controlcenter.png region at x800-1455,y20-689 shows all four glyphs centered and high-contrast, so this is a test-coverage risk, not a current visual defect. Fix: parameterize the existing multi-scale assertion across all four toggles, including the procedural Focus path, and assert a contrast floor against the measured fill colors.

what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a visible lock-preview exit and prove it works through keyboard/pointer classification while keeping the preview non-security; add a visible focus ring plus Enter/Space activation for classified controls only when the island already has focus, with focused tests; parameterize the existing multi-scale icon test across Wi-Fi, Focus, Bluetooth and NightLight with coverage, centroid and contrast assertions; then verify live pointer/focus behavior under the owner's explicit harness.
